tfn.s: Johnston's garden used to get more sun than it does now.
tfn.why: The text says: “Before, the sun used to come around here and it was lovely.”

tfn.s: The politicians who supported the project have visited his garden.
tfn.why: The text says the politicians “will not come to his garden to look at it”.

tfn.s: The 315 data centres have asked for more power than Britain normally uses on a cold winter day.
tfn.why: The text says they have asked for “far more power than the country normally uses on a cold winter day”.

tfn.s: The Newport data centre will employ more than 100 people.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not give a number of jobs for the Newport centre.

tfn.s: The number 315 shows how much electricity the centres are using.
tfn.why: The text says: “That number is a request, not a measurement.”

speak.title: Role-play: a data centre next door
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: A company wants to build a data centre behind your street. Tell the company what worries you, such as noise, fumes or lost sunlight. Ask for changes before you will agree.

b.text: You want to build the data centre. Explain the benefits, such as jobs. Listen to the resident, then offer one or two changes. You cannot agree to everything.

phrases: I'm really worried about the noise.
That's not good enough for us.
I'd like to hear more about the jobs.
We're happy to listen to your concerns.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you reach an agreement, and was it fair to the people living nearby?
